packageRules.description: NEVER automerge a Pulumi provider, at any version increment, and keep them in one pull request. AUTOMERGE: not pending a gate signal — there is none to wait for, and deliberately will not be. Producing the preview that would justify one means installing and EXECUTING the proposed package with ESC-resolved production credentials, which is why the Pulumi Cloud trigger `paths` exclude dependency manifests (see src/pulumi-cloud/deployment-settings.ts and design D6). A reviewer merges these after running `pulumi preview` themselves. GROUPING: this is NOISE REDUCTION, not a coupling claim. Measured — every provider requires `@pulumi/pulumi` with a lower bound only (`^3.142.0` against the `^3.234.0` in use) and none depends on another, so upgrading one alone builds fine and this group may be split at any time. It exists because `group:pulumi` turned out NOT to group them (six separate pull requests on the first Renovate run) and because every one of them is reviewed by hand, so six is six times the opening and closing.

Opt out of the organization preset's lock file maintenance automerge. Every Pulumi provider is declared with a caret range (`@pulumi/gcp ^9.22.0`, …), so refreshing the lock moves them to newer minors — the very updates the rule above keeps for a reviewer who has run `pulumi preview`. Automerging the refresh would ship those provider versions without that preview. Lock file maintenance stays proposed and is merged by hand.

HOLD typescript below 7 until Pulumi supports it. TypeScript 7 is the native (Go) compiler and its npm package ships no JavaScript API — `require('typescript').transpileModule` and `createProgram` are undefined — while Pulumi runs this program through ts-node, which is built on exactly that API. `@pulumi/pulumi` states it as a peer range, `typescript: ">= 3.8.3 < 7"` (3.265.0), so the TypeScript 7 pull request could not even install (`npm ci` ERESOLVE). This is a cap on a known-incompatible major, not a pin: minor and patch updates within 5.x still flow. REMOVE THIS RULE when `@pulumi/pulumi` widens that peer range — at that point the upgrade also needs the tsconfig migration frontend went through (TypeScript 6 removed `moduleResolution: node` and `baseUrl`, and changed the `strict` and `types` defaults).

NEVER propose our own application images. These are the tags pinned in k8s/namespaces/*/overlays/*/kustomization.yaml, and ArgoCD syncs from those overlays — so changing a `newTag` IS a deployment, not a dependency bump. They already have an owner: bump-prod-pin.yml moves the tag and its `app.kubernetes.io/version` label in lock-step and validates the result. A pull request here would propose shipping a version nobody decided to release; an automerged one would ship it unattended. Renovate's first run reported `No docker auth found` and ten failed lookups against this registry — that error is a SYMPTOM. Do NOT fix it by giving Renovate registry credentials: that would enable exactly the updates this rule exists to prevent. `enabled: false` rather than `ignorePaths` so they stay on the dependency dashboard as disabled-with-an-update-available, which makes an overlay left behind by a release visible. Third-party images are unaffected — every `images:` entry in this org is ours, and third-party ones appear as inline `image:` fields that the `kubernetes` manager still handles.  GLOB SHAPE: the trailing `/**` is load-bearing and must not be collapsed to `liverty-music-**`. Renovate parses these with minimatch, where `*` and a segment-internal `**` both stop at a `/` (https://docs.renovatebot.com/string-pattern-matching/), so `liverty-music-**` matches the project segment alone and NEVER `liverty-music-prod/backend/api`. It was written that way first, and the rule was inert: the dependency dashboard kept reporting ten failed lookups against this registry, which is how the mistake surfaced. See design D7.
